# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
# value loss is measured.
NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"

# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
LR="${LR:-1e-6}"

# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
# incident was about.
CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1

# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
#
# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"

# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"

RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"

mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"

# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install, and the value head's initial
# weights are exactly what ${SLIME_HOME}/.../model_provider.py says here.
MODEL_PROVIDER="${SLIME_HOME}/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py"
test -f "${MODEL_PROVIDER}" || {
    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${MODEL_PROVIDER}" >&2
    exit 1
}
echo "=== value head initialisation in effect (bundled slime) ==="
# Grep the whole file rather than a line range: the fixed and defective copies
# carry different comment blocks, so the decisive line is not at a fixed line
# number in both, and a range would print nothing for one of them.
grep -n "self\.weight\.data\.\(zero_\|normal_\)" "${MODEL_PROVIDER}" || true
echo

# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
fi
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
fi
# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
    fi
}
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
fi
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"

# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
    --input-key prompt
    --label-key label
    --rollout-shuffle
    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
    --rollout-temperature 1.0
    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --balance-data
    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
)

PPO_ARGS=(
    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
    --gamma 1.0
    --lambd 1.0
    --eps-clip 0.2
    --value-clip 0.2
    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
)

PERF_ARGS=(
    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
    --context-parallel-size 1
    --recompute-granularity full
    --recompute-method uniform
    --recompute-num-layers 1
    --use-dynamic-batch-size
    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
)
# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
fi

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
    --optimizer adam
    --lr "${LR}"
    --lr-decay-style constant
    --weight-decay 0.0
    --adam-beta1 0.9
    --adam-beta2 0.95
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
)

# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
#
# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
#
# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
EVAL_ARGS=()
if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
eval:
  datasets:
    - name: et_val
      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
    - name: et_test
      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
YAML
    EVAL_ARGS=(
        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
        --eval-max-response-len 2048
        --eval-temperature 1.0
        --log-passrate
        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
    )
fi

MISC_ARGS=(
    --attention-dropout 0.0
    --hidden-dropout 0.0
    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
    --attention-backend flash
    --seed 1234
)

# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
megatron:
  - name: stage-a-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
  - name: stage-a-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
YAML

# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
#
#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded", the thing this case is about. The
#              actor resumes from Stage A's Megatron checkpoint; the critic's
#              backbone comes from the base model, because a saved actor
#              checkpoint carries no value head, so the value head exists only
#              because LinearForLastLayer.__init__ just created it. That
#              constructor is the whole of the behaviour under test.
#
#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included. The critic's saved
#              output layer is already [1, hidden_size], so this is an ordinary
#              resumption and no value head is constructed afresh -- which is
#              exactly right: the measurement belongs to the fresh entry, and
#              the first attempt's log already holds it.
STAGE_B_RESUME=0
if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
fi

if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
else
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
fi

cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
megatron:
  - name: stage-b-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
  - name: stage-b-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
YAML

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

ray start --head \
    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
    --disable-usage-stats \
    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT

# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
HAS_NVLINK=0
[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1

RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
  \"env_vars\": {
    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
  }
}"

submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
    local log="$1"; shift
    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
    ray job submit \
        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
        --colocate \
        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
}

# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read
    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.
    local tag="$1"
    local dst="${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs"
    mkdir -p "${dst}"
    grep -rl "critic-step" "${RAY_TMP}"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
        cp -f "${f}" "${dst}/$(basename "$(dirname "${f}")")_$(basename "${f}")" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A
echo
echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"
# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for
# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.
if [ "${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    echo "SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it."
else
    submit "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
        --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" \
        --load "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
        --save-interval 1 \
        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
        --num-critic-only-steps 0
    collect_worker_logs stage_a
fi

echo
echo "checkpoint written by Stage A:"
ls -1 "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" 2>/dev/null || true
test -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" || {
    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B
echo
echo "############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############"
# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args
# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far
# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the
# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs
# is the one Stage A already produced.
#
# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.
# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron
# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts
# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones ("total number of
# iterations do not match"). The flag says "use the command line, not the
# checkpoint", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that
# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.
STAGE_B_ARGS=(
    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"
    --load "${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}"
    --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
    --save-interval "$([ "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ] && echo "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" || echo 1000)"
    --override-opt-param-scheduler
    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
)

STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"
if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.
    n=1
    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
    STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log"
    echo "resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}" \
         "(iteration $(cat "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}"
    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start
    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play
    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,
    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.
else
    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is
    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh
    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).
    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)
fi

submit "${STAGE_B_LOG}" "${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}" "${EVAL_ARGS[@]+"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}"}"
collect_worker_logs stage_b

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict
echo
echo "############ critic warmup value loss ############"
python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log" \
    --warmup-steps "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" \
    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json"

python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

echo
echo "artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:"
ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}"

"""Multi-turn Endless Terminals rollout for slime.

Wired in via:
    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
    --custom-rm-path                et.rollout.reward_func

One sample == one terminal episode. Each turn the policy emits exactly one
`<command>...</command>` (or `<action>done</action>`); the command runs in the
episode's private shell and the harness-formatted result is appended to the
context as a non-trainable user turn. The episode reward is the task's own
pytest verifier: 1.0 or 0.0, awarded once at the end of the episode.

The system prompt below is copied verbatim from the Endless Terminals reference
transcripts (`solution/o3_summary.json`), as is the observation wording, so the
policy sees the same interface the dataset was built against.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
import re

from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
from slime.utils.http_utils import post
from slime.utils.types import Sample

from et.sandbox import Episode, check_exec_capable

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a highly capable Linux terminal agent operating strictly via a single-shell-command interface.
Goal: complete the user's task.

Rules:
- Output exactly one of the following per turn:
  1) <command>THE_SINGLE_SHELL_COMMAND</command>
  OR
  2) <action>done</action>
- Don't use interactive commands and confirmations; use non-interactive flags.
- Prefer simple, robust CLI tools; write files explicitly when needed.
- If you believe the task is solved, emit <action>done</action>.
- Hint: you might want to run commands interactively to see the output and then write the command. Don't just pipe the commands.
- Only your first command in command tags will be executed. So don't respond with multiple commands.
- Hint: Verify your solution once you are done. Eg: you can use cat to see the input and the output.
- Do not just write long bash scripts. Write the commands that you would write in a terminal."""

DATA_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_DATA_ROOT", "/tmp/et_prompts")
# Must allow execution, so not under /dev/shm -- see et.sandbox.check_exec_capable.
SCRATCH_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_SCRATCH", "/tmp/et_episodes")
MAX_TURNS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_TURNS", "8"))
MAX_NEW_TOKENS_PER_TURN = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS", "512"))
CMD_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_CMD_TIMEOUT", "20"))
MAX_OBS_CHARS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS", "1500"))
# Hard ceiling on one episode, covering everything: generation, the shell, the
# verifier and teardown. Every individual step is already bounded, yet the run
# still hung -- slime builds its HTTP client with `httpx.Timeout(None)`, so a
# `/generate` that never comes back waits forever, and asyncio's
# `Process.wait()` has its own way of never resolving (see sandbox.REAP_TIMEOUT).
# Both drivers await every episode before returning, so one episode that never
# finishes stalls the entire rollout rather than failing it. The default is
# deliberately far above any legitimate episode -- 6 turns of generation plus
# 6x20s of commands plus a 180s verifier -- so this only ever fires on a hang.
EPISODE_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_EPISODE_TIMEOUT", "900"))

STOP_STRINGS = ["</command>", "</action>"]
_OBS_SENTINEL = "@@ET_OBSERVATION@@"

_COMMAND_RE = re.compile(r"<command>(.*?)(?:</command>|\Z)", re.DOTALL)
_ACTION_RE = re.compile(r"<action>\s*done\s*</action>", re.IGNORECASE)


class _Chat:
    """Derives the chat-template glue once, without hardcoding ChatML.

    `head` is the token prefix the policy generates from. `tail` is the text
    that must follow a generated assistant turn in order to inject one user
    turn and re-open the assistant turn.
    """

    def __init__(self, tokenizer) -> None:
        kwargs = {"tokenize": False, "add_generation_prompt": True, "enable_thinking": False}
        probe_msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": "S"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}]
        head = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(probe_msgs, **kwargs)
        full = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            probe_msgs
            + [{"role": "assistant", "content": "A"}, {"role": "user", "content": _OBS_SENTINEL}],
            **kwargs,
        )
        prefix = os.path.commonprefix([head, full])
        assert full[len(prefix) : len(prefix) + 1] == "A", "unexpected chat template shape"
        self._tail = full[len(prefix) + 1 :]
        assert _OBS_SENTINEL in self._tail, "could not locate the observation slot in the chat template"
        self._kwargs = kwargs

    def prompt(self, tokenizer, instruction: str) -> str:
        return tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": instruction}],
            **self._kwargs,
        )

    def observation(self, text: str) -> str:
        return self._tail.replace(_OBS_SENTINEL, text)


_CHAT: _Chat | None = None
_SCRATCH_CHECKED = False


def _chat(tokenizer) -> _Chat:
    global _CHAT
    if _CHAT is None:
        _CHAT = _Chat(tokenizer)
    return _CHAT


def _check_scratch_once() -> None:
    global _SCRATCH_CHECKED
    if not _SCRATCH_CHECKED:
        check_exec_capable(SCRATCH_ROOT)
        _SCRATCH_CHECKED = True


def parse_action(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Return ("command", cmd) / ("done", None) / ("invalid", None).

    Mirrors the harness rule "only your first command in command tags will be
    executed": whichever of `<command>` / `<action>` appears first wins.
    """
    cmd_match = _COMMAND_RE.search(text)
    act_match = _ACTION_RE.search(text)
    if act_match and (cmd_match is None or act_match.start() < cmd_match.start()):
        return "done", None
    if cmd_match:
        cmd = cmd_match.group(1).strip()
        return ("command", cmd) if cmd else ("invalid", None)
    return "invalid", None


def _abort(args, sample: Sample, turns: int, **extra) -> Sample:
    """Finish a sample that is giving up, with every field slime will index.

    `_convert_samples_to_train_data` repeatedly decides whether an optional
    per-sample field is present by looking at `samples[0]` alone, and then
    indexes *every* sample in the batch. An episode that gives up while its
    neighbours complete normally is therefore not a local failure -- it takes
    down the whole rollout, from a traceback that names slime rather than this
    file. Three such fields exist on this path:

      * `reward` -- eval metrics take `sum(rewards) / len(rewards)` over the
        split (rollout_metrics.py:232), so one `None` raises;
      * `metadata["round_number"]` -- ray/rollout.py:382, `KeyError`;
      * `rollout_log_probs` -- ray/rollout.py:386, and a sample that never got
        a single response token still has `None` there, which surfaces much
        later as `TypeError: must be real number, not NoneType` inside
        `torch.as_tensor`.

    The last one is why an aborted episode with nothing generated is given one
    end-of-text token, appended as *non-trainable*: that is slime's own
    supported way to add tokens that carry no gradient, so every per-sample
    list ends up present, mutually consistent and zero-weighted rather than
    absent. Centralising the giving-up paths here is the only way to keep all
    of this true as new ones get added.
    """
    sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
    sample.reward = 0.0
    if sample.response_length == 0:
        eos = GenerateState(args).tokenizer.eos_token_id
        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=[eos], trainable=False, text="")
    sample.metadata = {
        **(sample.metadata or {}),
        "et_task": sample.label,
        "round_number": turns,
        **extra,
    }
    return sample


def _turns_so_far(sample: Sample) -> int:
    """How many turns the episode had started when it was interrupted.

    `_generate` stamps the turn counter into metadata as it goes, precisely so
    that a timeout or an exception -- which unwinds past every local variable --
    still has a truthful number to report.
    """
    return int((sample.metadata or {}).get("round_number", 0))


async def generate(args, sample: Sample, sampling_params) -> Sample:
    """slime hook: `custom_generate_function_path`. Never raises, always returns.

    Both drivers that call this -- `generate_rollout` and `eval_rollout` --
    launch every episode as a task and then `await` them through
    `asyncio.as_completed`, so an episode that raises discards the entire
    rollout and an episode that hangs stalls it indefinitely. Both have
    happened: a task printing a line longer than asyncio's stream limit threw
    away several hundred finished episodes, and a task whose instructions are
    to leave `sleep 1000` and `yes` running in the background froze an eval at
    1199 of 1200 episodes.

    Nothing one episode can do is worth a whole rollout, so an episode that
    fails or stops making progress is reported the way a setup failure already
    is: aborted, reward 0, flagged in metadata so it is visible afterwards
    rather than silently absorbed.
    """
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(_generate(args, sample, sampling_params), timeout=EPISODE_TIMEOUT)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the critic's warmup value loss from a slime training log.

slime reports per-optimizer-step training metrics only on stdout, via
`slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`:

    logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")

so for the critic the lines look like

    critic-step 0: {'train/critic-value_loss': 5.91, 'train/critic-value_clipfrac': 0.0, ...}

Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:

    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}

Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.

There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.

Usage:
    python3 tools/parse_value_loss.py train.log --warmup-steps 2 --out summary.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import json
import re
import sys

STEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s\]])(?P<role>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*-)?step\s+(?P<step>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")

# `<label> <id>: {...}` for any label that is not a `step` line, i.e. the
# rollout-level metrics. Anchored on " - " so it matches the logger's
# "<file>.py:<line> - " prefix and not arbitrary prose.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline check: an aborted episode must survive slime's train-data builder.

`_convert_samples_to_train_data` decides whether an optional per-sample field
is present by looking at `samples[0]` alone, and then indexes *every* sample in
the batch. So the shape that breaks is a batch mixing one normal episode with
one that gave up -- which is exactly what a rollout looks like whenever SGLang
aborts a straggler. The failure surfaces as a `KeyError` or a `TypeError` deep
inside slime, an hour into a run, and costs the whole rollout.

Reproducing that shape here costs seconds. Run it after touching any giving-up
path in `et/rollout.py`:

    python3 tools/check_abort_path.py    # inside the slime image

No GPU, no model and no network: the tokenizer is stubbed out, because the only
thing `_abort` wants from it is an end-of-text id.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from argparse import Namespace

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

import et.rollout as R  # noqa: E402
from slime.observability.rollout_data_utils import tensorize_rollout_data_for_training  # noqa: E402
from slime.utils.types import Sample  # noqa: E402

EOS = 151645  # Qwen3's <|im_end|>; any valid id would do, it is never trained on


class _FakeTokenizer:
    eos_token_id = EOS


class _FakeState:
    """Stands in for slime's `GenerateState`, which would load a real tokenizer."""

    def __init__(self, args):
        self.tokenizer = _FakeTokenizer()


R.GenerateState = _FakeState

ARGS = Namespace(
    rollout_top_p=1.0,
    rollout_max_response_len=2048,
    partial_rollout=False,
    use_rollout_routing_replay=False,
)


def normal_sample(index: int) -> Sample:
    """An episode that ran a turn and was scored -- opens every slime gate."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_normal")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[10, 11], log_probs=[-0.1, -0.2], trainable=True, text="a")
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[12], trainable=False, text="obs")
    sample.reward = 1.0
    sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED
    sample.metadata = {"round_number": 1, "et_task": "task_normal"}
    return sample


def aborted_sample(index: int, turns: int) -> Sample:
    """An episode that gave up -- before generating anything, or after a turn."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_aborted")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    if turns:
        sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[20], log_probs=[-0.3], trainable=True, text="b")
    return R._abort(ARGS, sample, turns, et_finish="sglang_abort")


def main() -> int:
    failures: list[str] = []

    for turns in (0, 1):
        sample = aborted_sample(1, turns)
        where = f"abort after {turns} turn(s)"
        if sample.reward is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: reward is None (slime's eval metrics average over the whole split)")
        if not sample.metadata or "round_number" not in sample.metadata:
            failures.append(f"{where}: metadata['round_number'] missing (ray/rollout.py:382)")
        if sample.rollout_log_probs is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: rollout_log_probs is None (ray/rollout.py:386)")
        elif len(sample.rollout_log_probs) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(
                f"{where}: rollout_log_probs {len(sample.rollout_log_probs)} "
                f"!= response_length {sample.response_length}"
            )
        if sample.loss_mask is None or len(sample.loss_mask) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(f"{where}: loss_mask inconsistent with response_length")
        if turns == 0 and sum(sample.loss_mask or []):
            failures.append(f"{where}: an episode that generated nothing must contribute no trainable token")
        print(
            f"  {where}: response_length={sample.response_length} loss_mask={sample.loss_mask} "
            f"log_probs={sample.rollout_log_probs} round_number={sample.metadata.get('round_number')}"
        )

    # The batch slime actually builds: a normal sample first, so every optional
    # field's gate opens on `samples[0]`, then the ones that gave up.
    samples = [normal_sample(0), aborted_sample(1, 0), aborted_sample(2, 1)]
    for sample in samples:
        if sample.loss_mask is None:  # slime does this itself, before the gates
            sample.loss_mask = [1] * sample.response_length

    train_data = {
        "tokens": [s.tokens for s in samples],
        "response_lengths": [s.response_length for s in samples],
        "rewards": [s.reward for s in samples],
        "loss_masks": [s.loss_mask for s in samples],
    }
    if samples[0].metadata and "round_number" in samples[0].metadata:
        try:
            train_data["round_number"] = [s.metadata["round_number"] for s in samples]
        except KeyError as exc:
            failures.append(f"round_number gate: KeyError {exc}")
    if samples[0].rollout_log_probs is not None:
        train_data["rollout_log_probs"] = [s.rollout_log_probs for s in samples]
    # These three gates must stay shut: this rollout never populates them, and a
    # sample that opened one would take the batch down the same way.
    for field in ("rollout_routed_experts", "train_metadata", "teacher_log_probs"):
        if getattr(samples[0], field, None) is not None:
            failures.append(f"{field} gate unexpectedly open")

    try:
        tensorize_rollout_data_for_training(train_data)
        print("  tensorize: OK")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        failures.append(f"tensorize: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    if failures:
        print("\nFAIL")
        for failure in failures:
            print("  -", failure)
        return 1
    print("\nPASS: a batch mixing normal and aborted episodes survives slime's train-data builder")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

slime reports per-optimizer-step training metrics only on stdout, via

so for the critic the lines look like

    critic-step 0: {'train/critic-value_loss': 5.91, 'train/critic-value_clipfrac': 0.0, ...}

Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:

    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}

Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.

There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.

Usage:
    python3 tools/parse_value_loss.py train.log --warmup-steps 2 --out summary.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import json
import re
import sys

STEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s\]])(?P<role>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*-)?step\s+(?P<step>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")

# `<label> <id>: {...}` for any label that is not a `step` line, i.e. the
# rollout-level metrics. Anchored on " - " so it matches the logger's
# "<file>.py:<line> - " prefix and not arbitrary prose.
ROLLOUT_RE = re.compile(r" - (?P<label>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+(?P<id>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")


def _coerce(value):
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _payload(text: str) -> dict | None:
    try:
        payload = ast.literal_eval(text)
    except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
        return None
    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None


def parse(paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Return one record per metric line, tagged `step` or `rollout`."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    for path in paths:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                line = line.rstrip("\n")
                m = STEP_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    role = (m.group("role") or "").rstrip("-") or "actor"
                    records.append(
                        {"kind": "step", "role": role, "step": int(m.group("step")), "metrics": payload}
                    )
                    continue
                m = ROLLOUT_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    records.append(
                        {
                            "kind": "rollout",
                            "label": m.group("label"),
                            "step": int(m.group("id")),
                            "metrics": payload,
                        }
                    )
    return records


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--warmup-steps",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="number of leading critic optimizer steps to average over (0 = all critic steps)",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    records = parse(args.logs)

    critic_steps = []
    for rec in records:
        if rec["kind"] != "step":
            continue
        hit = next((k for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_loss")), None)
        if hit is None:
            continue
        value = _coerce(rec["metrics"][hit])
        if value is None:
            continue
        critic_steps.append(
            {
                "step": rec["step"],
                "value_loss": value,
                "value_clipfrac": _coerce(
                    next((rec["metrics"][k] for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_clipfrac")), None)
                ),
            }
        )
    critic_steps.sort(key=lambda r: r["step"])

    rewards = []
    for rec in records:
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items():
            if "reward" in key and not key.endswith(("_std", "_max", "_min")):
                coerced = _coerce(value)
                if coerced is not None:
                    rewards.append({"step": rec["step"], "key": key, "value": coerced})

    # Evidence that episodes were really generated in this stage, independent of
    # whether the actor trained: the RolloutManager reports response-length
    # statistics once per rollout. A stage that generated nothing has neither.
    #
    # Only `rollout/response_len/mean` (the RolloutManager's `perf N:` line) is
    # averaged. slime also emits `rollout/response_lengths` from the actor side,
    # but it is a *different* quantity -- it counts the tokens the trainer sees,
    # including the observation turns fed back into the context, so it runs ~70%
    # higher. Averaging the two together produced a blended figure that meant
    # nothing and was not comparable between stages, since the actor-side metric
    # only exists on rollouts where the actor trains.
    rollout_ids = {rec["step"] for rec in records if rec["kind"] == "rollout"}
    response_lens = [
        _coerce(value)
        for rec in records
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items()
        if key.endswith("response_len/mean")
    ]
    response_lens = [v for v in response_lens if v is not None]

    window = critic_steps[: args.warmup_steps] if args.warmup_steps > 0 else critic_steps
    losses = [r["value_loss"] for r in window]

    summary = {
        "n_critic_steps": len(critic_steps),
        "rollouts_generated": len(rollout_ids),
        "mean_response_len": (sum(response_lens) / len(response_lens)) if response_lens else None,
        "warmup_window": len(window),
        "critic_steps": critic_steps,
        "first_value_loss": critic_steps[0]["value_loss"] if critic_steps else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_mean": (sum(losses) / len(losses)) if losses else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_max": max(losses) if losses else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_min": min(losses) if losses else None,
        "rewards": rewards[:50],
        "mean_reward": (sum(r["value"] for r in rewards) / len(rewards)) if rewards else None,
    }

    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)

    print(f"critic optimizer steps found: {summary['n_critic_steps']}")
    if not critic_steps:
        print("NO value_loss METRICS FOUND -- the critic never took an optimizer step.", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Check that --advantage-estimator ppo is set and that training reached the critic.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(f"{'step':>6}  {'value_loss':>14}  {'value_clipfrac':>14}")
    for rec in critic_steps:
        clip = "n/a" if rec["value_clipfrac"] is None else f"{rec['value_clipfrac']:.4f}"
        print(f"{rec['step']:>6}  {rec['value_loss']:>14.6f}  {clip:>14}")
    print(f"\nwarmup window = first {summary['warmup_window']} critic step(s)")
    print(f"warmup value_loss mean = {summary['warmup_value_loss_mean']:.6f}")
    print(f"rollouts generated = {summary['rollouts_generated']}", end="")
    if summary["mean_response_len"] is not None:
        print(f" (mean response {summary['mean_response_len']:.1f} tokens)", end="")
    print()
    if summary["mean_reward"] is not None:
        print(f"mean reward (episode pass rate) ~= {summary['mean_reward']:.4f}")
    return 0

    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline check: an aborted episode must survive slime's train-data builder.

`_convert_samples_to_train_data` decides whether an optional per-sample field
is present by looking at `samples[0]` alone, and then indexes *every* sample in
the batch. So the shape that breaks is a batch mixing one normal episode with
one that gave up -- which is exactly what a rollout looks like whenever SGLang
aborts a straggler. The failure surfaces as a `KeyError` or a `TypeError` deep
inside slime, an hour into a run, and costs the whole rollout.

Reproducing that shape here costs seconds. Run it after touching any giving-up
path in `et/rollout.py`:

    python3 tools/check_abort_path.py    # inside the slime image

No GPU, no model and no network: the tokenizer is stubbed out, because the only
thing `_abort` wants from it is an end-of-text id.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from argparse import Namespace

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

import et.rollout as R  # noqa: E402
from slime.observability.rollout_data_utils import tensorize_rollout_data_for_training  # noqa: E402
from slime.utils.types import Sample  # noqa: E402

EOS = 151645  # Qwen3's <|im_end|>; any valid id would do, it is never trained on


class _FakeTokenizer:
    eos_token_id = EOS


class _FakeState:
    """Stands in for slime's `GenerateState`, which would load a real tokenizer."""

    def __init__(self, args):
        self.tokenizer = _FakeTokenizer()


R.GenerateState = _FakeState

ARGS = Namespace(
    rollout_top_p=1.0,
    rollout_max_response_len=2048,
    partial_rollout=False,
    use_rollout_routing_replay=False,
)


def normal_sample(index: int) -> Sample:
    """An episode that ran a turn and was scored -- opens every slime gate."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_normal")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[10, 11], log_probs=[-0.1, -0.2], trainable=True, text="a")
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[12], trainable=False, text="obs")
    sample.reward = 1.0
    sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED
    sample.metadata = {"round_number": 1, "et_task": "task_normal"}
    return sample


def aborted_sample(index: int, turns: int) -> Sample:
    """An episode that gave up -- before generating anything, or after a turn."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_aborted")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    if turns:
        sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[20], log_probs=[-0.3], trainable=True, text="b")
    return R._abort(ARGS, sample, turns, et_finish="sglang_abort")


def main() -> int:
    failures: list[str] = []

    for turns in (0, 1):
        sample = aborted_sample(1, turns)
        where = f"abort after {turns} turn(s)"
        if sample.reward is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: reward is None (slime's eval metrics average over the whole split)")
        if not sample.metadata or "round_number" not in sample.metadata:
            failures.append(f"{where}: metadata['round_number'] missing (ray/rollout.py:382)")
        if sample.rollout_log_probs is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: rollout_log_probs is None (ray/rollout.py:386)")
        elif len(sample.rollout_log_probs) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(
                f"{where}: rollout_log_probs {len(sample.rollout_log_probs)} "
                f"!= response_length {sample.response_length}"
            )
        if sample.loss_mask is None or len(sample.loss_mask) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(f"{where}: loss_mask inconsistent with response_length")
        if turns == 0 and sum(sample.loss_mask or []):
            failures.append(f"{where}: an episode that generated nothing must contribute no trainable token")
        print(
            f"  {where}: response_length={sample.response_length} loss_mask={sample.loss_mask} "
            f"log_probs={sample.rollout_log_probs} round_number={sample.metadata.get('round_number')}"
        )

    # The batch slime actually builds: a normal sample first, so every optional
    # field's gate opens on `samples[0]`, then the ones that gave up.
    samples = [normal_sample(0), aborted_sample(1, 0), aborted_sample(2, 1)]
    for sample in samples:
        if sample.loss_mask is None:  # slime does this itself, before the gates
            sample.loss_mask = [1] * sample.response_length

    train_data = {
        "tokens": [s.tokens for s in samples],
        "response_lengths": [s.response_length for s in samples],
        "rewards": [s.reward for s in samples],
        "loss_masks": [s.loss_mask for s in samples],
    }
    if samples[0].metadata and "round_number" in samples[0].metadata:
        try:
            train_data["round_number"] = [s.metadata["round_number"] for s in samples]
        except KeyError as exc:
            failures.append(f"round_number gate: KeyError {exc}")
    if samples[0].rollout_log_probs is not None:
        train_data["rollout_log_probs"] = [s.rollout_log_probs for s in samples]
    # These three gates must stay shut: this rollout never populates them, and a
    # sample that opened one would take the batch down the same way.
    for field in ("rollout_routed_experts", "train_metadata", "teacher_log_probs"):
        if getattr(samples[0], field, None) is not None:
            failures.append(f"{field} gate unexpectedly open")

    try:
        tensorize_rollout_data_for_training(train_data)
        print("  tensorize: OK")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        failures.append(f"tensorize: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    if failures:
        print("\nFAIL")
        for failure in failures:
            print("  -", failure)

    """An episode that ran a turn and was scored -- opens every slime gate."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_normal")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[10, 11], log_probs=[-0.1, -0.2], trainable=True, text="a")
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[12], trainable=False, text="obs")
    sample.reward = 1.0
    sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED
    sample.metadata = {"round_number": 1, "et_task": "task_normal"}
    return sample


def aborted_sample(index: int, turns: int) -> Sample:
    """An episode that gave up -- before generating anything, or after a turn."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_aborted")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    if turns:
        sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[20], log_probs=[-0.3], trainable=True, text="b")
    return R._abort(ARGS, sample, turns, et_finish="sglang_abort")


def main() -> int:
    failures: list[str] = []

    for turns in (0, 1):
        sample = aborted_sample(1, turns)
        where = f"abort after {turns} turn(s)"
        if sample.reward is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: reward is None (slime's eval metrics average over the whole split)")
        if not sample.metadata or "round_number" not in sample.metadata:
            failures.append(f"{where}: metadata['round_number'] missing (ray/rollout.py:382)")
        if sample.rollout_log_probs is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: rollout_log_probs is None (ray/rollout.py:386)")
        elif len(sample.rollout_log_probs) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(
                f"{where}: rollout_log_probs {len(sample.rollout_log_probs)} "
                f"!= response_length {sample.response_length}"
            )
        if sample.loss_mask is None or len(sample.loss_mask) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(f"{where}: loss_mask inconsistent with response_length")
        if turns == 0 and sum(sample.loss_mask or []):
            failures.append(f"{where}: an episode that generated nothing must contribute no trainable token")
        print(
            f"  {where}: response_length={sample.response_length} loss_mask={sample.loss_mask} "
            f"log_probs={sample.rollout_log_probs} round_number={sample.metadata.get('round_number')}"
        )

    # The batch slime actually builds: a normal sample first, so every optional
    # field's gate opens on `samples[0]`, then the ones that gave up.
    samples = [normal_sample(0), aborted_sample(1, 0), aborted_sample(2, 1)]
    for sample in samples:
        if sample.loss_mask is None:  # slime does this itself, before the gates
            sample.loss_mask = [1] * sample.response_length

    train_data = {
        "tokens": [s.tokens for s in samples],
        "response_lengths": [s.response_length for s in samples],
        "rewards": [s.reward for s in samples],
        "loss_masks": [s.loss_mask for s in samples],
    }
    if samples[0].metadata and "round_number" in samples[0].metadata:
        try:
            train_data["round_number"] = [s.metadata["round_number"] for s in samples]
        except KeyError as exc:
            failures.append(f"round_number gate: KeyError {exc}")
    if samples[0].rollout_log_probs is not None:
        train_data["rollout_log_probs"] = [s.rollout_log_probs for s in samples]
    # These three gates must stay shut: this rollout never populates them, and a
    # sample that opened one would take the batch down the same way.
    for field in ("rollout_routed_experts", "train_metadata", "teacher_log_probs"):
        if getattr(samples[0], field, None) is not None:
            failures.append(f"{field} gate unexpectedly open")

    try:
        tensorize_rollout_data_for_training(train_data)
        print("  tensorize: OK")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        failures.append(f"tensorize: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    if failures:
        print("\nFAIL")
        for failure in failures:
            print("  -", failure)
        return 1
    print("\nPASS: a batch mixing normal and aborted episodes survives slime's train-data builder")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dump every held-out episode's reward, keyed by task, as the eval runs.

slime's own eval logging reports means: `eval/et_test` is the pass rate over the
whole split, and that is all it keeps. A mean is not enough to compare two
training runs here. The two arms are scored on the *same* tasks, so the right
test is a paired one -- per task, did this arm solve it more often than the
other? -- and a paired test needs the per-task numbers, which the mean has
already thrown away. Across a 300-task split an unpaired comparison of two
~6% pass rates needs several times the episodes to reach the same power,
because almost all of the variance between the arms' means is task difficulty
that is identical on both sides and cancels when you subtract per task.

So this hook writes one JSONL row per episode next to the run's other
artifacts. It returns a falsy value on purpose: slime treats a truthy return as
"the custom logger handled it", and the aggregate lines are still wanted.

Wired in by run.sh as
`--custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

# Written by the RolloutManager actor, not by the driver, so the path has to
# travel through the Ray runtime env rather than being inherited from run.sh.
DUMP_DIR = os.environ.get("ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR", "")


def _status(sample) -> str:
    status = getattr(sample, "status", None)
    return getattr(status, "value", str(status))


def _reward(sample, fallback):
    """The scalar reward, whatever shape the sample carries it in.

    slime allows `Sample.reward` to be a dict (`--reward-key` picks a field out
    of it). `data[name]["rewards"]` has already been resolved to scalars, so it
    is the authoritative source; the sample is only consulted if the two lists
    somehow fail to line up.
    """
    if fallback is not None:
        return fallback
    reward = getattr(sample, "reward", None)
    return reward if not isinstance(reward, dict) else None


def log_eval_rollout_data(rollout_id, args, data, extra_metrics=None):  # noqa: ARG001
    """slime hook: `custom_eval_rollout_log_function_path`.

    Returns None so slime goes on to emit its own aggregate `eval N:` line --
    this adds a record, it does not replace one.
    """
    if not DUMP_DIR:
        return None
    os.makedirs(DUMP_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(DUMP_DIR, f"eval_rollout_{rollout_id:04d}.jsonl")

    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for name, payload in data.items():
            samples = payload.get("samples") or []
            rewards = payload.get("rewards") or []
            for i, sample in enumerate(samples):
                row = {
                    "rollout_id": rollout_id,
                    "dataset": name,

                    # rows joinable and the comparison paired.

                    "index": getattr(sample, "index", None),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Split the admitted Endless Terminals prompt set into train / val / test.

A run must train on one set of tasks and be scored on another, and the split
must be stable across runs, or a comparison between runs measures the split
instead of the change under study. So the split is a pure function of the
admitted task list and a seed: run this at any time and you get the same three
files.

Sizing (defaults) comes from a power calculation for the end-to-end held-out
pass-rate claim:

  test  300 tasks x 4 samples   Scored *paired* -- the same tasks and the same
                                per-task sample budget each time, so task
                                difficulty cancels out of the difference.
                                With a within-task correlation of ~0.6 that is
                                ~430 effective tasks, enough to resolve a 5-6
                                percentage-point difference in pass rate at
                                80% power. Going past 4 samples per task buys
                                almost nothing: at rho=0.6, k=8 is only 8%
                                better than k=4 for twice the generation.
  val   150 tasks x 2 samples   Used to decide when training has converged, so
                                that the stopping point is not chosen on the
                                test set.
  train everything else         ~1k tasks; at 16 episodes per rollout the
                                trainer sees each one about once per 65
                                rollouts.

Usage:
    python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts /tmp/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import random


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--prompts", required=True, help="endless_terminals.jsonl from et.build_dataset")
    ap.add_argument("--val-size", type=int, default=150)
    ap.add_argument("--test-size", type=int, default=300)
    # Fixed by default. A split that moved between runs would silently turn a
    # within-task comparison into a between-task one.
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261009)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    with open(args.prompts, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in fh if line.strip()]
    # Sort before shuffling: the input order is whatever the validation pass
    # happened to emit, and sorting makes the shuffle depend on the seed alone.
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["label"])

    if args.val_size + args.test_size >= len(rows):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{len(rows)} admitted tasks cannot supply a {args.val_size}+{args.test_size} holdout"
        )

    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    rng.shuffle(rows)
    test, val, train = (
        rows[: args.test_size],
        rows[args.test_size : args.test_size + args.val_size],
        rows[args.test_size + args.val_size :],
    )

    out_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.prompts))
    stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(args.prompts))[0]
    for name, part in (("train", train), ("val", val), ("test", test)):
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{stem}_{name}.jsonl")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for row in sorted(part, key=lambda r: r["label"]):
                fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        print(f"{name:>5}: {len(part):5d} tasks -> {path}")

    manifest = os.path.join(out_dir, "splits.json")
    with open(manifest, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(
            {
                "seed": args.seed,
                "n_admitted": len(rows),
                "train": sorted(r["label"] for r in train),
                "val": sorted(r["label"] for r in val),
                "test": sorted(r["label"] for r in test),
            },
            fh,
            indent=2,
        )
    print(f"manifest -> {manifest}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Split the admitted Endless Terminals prompt set into train / val / test.

A run must train on one set of tasks and be scored on another, and the split
must be stable across runs, or a comparison between runs measures the split
instead of the change under study. So the split is a pure function of the
admitted task list and a seed: run this at any time and you get the same three
files.

Sizing (defaults) comes from a power calculation for the end-to-end held-out
pass-rate claim:

  test  300 tasks x 4 samples   Scored *paired* -- the same tasks and the same
                                per-task sample budget each time, so task
                                difficulty cancels out of the difference.
                                With a within-task correlation of ~0.6 that is
                                ~430 effective tasks, enough to resolve a 5-6
                                percentage-point difference in pass rate at
                                80% power. Going past 4 samples per task buys
                                almost nothing: at rho=0.6, k=8 is only 8%
                                better than k=4 for twice the generation.
  val   150 tasks x 2 samples   Used to decide when training has converged, so
                                that the stopping point is not chosen on the
                                test set.
  train everything else         ~1k tasks; at 16 episodes per rollout the
                                trainer sees each one about once per 65
                                rollouts.

Usage:
    python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts /tmp/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import random


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--prompts", required=True, help="endless_terminals.jsonl from et.build_dataset")
    ap.add_argument("--val-size", type=int, default=150)
    ap.add_argument("--test-size", type=int, default=300)
    # Fixed by default. A split that moved between runs would silently turn a
    # within-task comparison into a between-task one.
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261009)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    with open(args.prompts, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in fh if line.strip()]
    # Sort before shuffling: the input order is whatever the validation pass
    # happened to emit, and sorting makes the shuffle depend on the seed alone.
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["label"])

    if args.val_size + args.test_size >= len(rows):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{len(rows)} admitted tasks cannot supply a {args.val_size}+{args.test_size} holdout"
        )

    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    rng.shuffle(rows)
    test, val, train = (
        rows[: args.test_size],
        rows[args.test_size : args.test_size + args.val_size],
        rows[args.test_size + args.val_size :],
    )

    out_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.prompts))
    stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(args.prompts))[0]
    for name, part in (("train", train), ("val", val), ("test", test)):
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{stem}_{name}.jsonl")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for row in sorted(part, key=lambda r: r["label"]):
                fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        print(f"{name:>5}: {len(part):5d} tasks -> {path}")

    manifest = os.path.join(out_dir, "splits.json")
    with open(manifest, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(
            {
                "seed": args.seed,
                "n_admitted": len(rows),
                "train": sorted(r["label"] for r in train),
                "val": sorted(r["label"] for r in val),
                "test": sorted(r["label"] for r in test),
            },
            fh,
            indent=2,
        )
    print(f"manifest -> {manifest}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

import argparse
import inspect
import re
from contextlib import nullcontext
from typing import Literal

import torch
from megatron.core import tensor_parallel
from megatron.core.models.gpt import GPTModel
from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import (
    get_gpt_decoder_block_spec,
    get_gpt_layer_local_spec,
    get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec,
)
from megatron.core.transformer.spec_utils import import_module
from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import TransformerConfig
from megatron.training.arguments import core_transformer_config_from_args

from slime.utils.misc import load_function

_INDEXER_DIRECT_SUBMODULE_NAMES = frozenset(
    {
        "wq_b",
        "wk",
        "k_norm",
        "weights_proj",
        "index_kpool_compress_ape",
        "index_kpool_compress_gate",
    }
)


def _is_indexer_parameter(name: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether *name* belongs to a DSA indexer.

    The GLM plugin exposes indexer projections directly under
    ``self_attention``. Megatron's upstream DSA implementation instead nests
    them under ``self_attention.core_attention.indexer``. Keep the ownership
    check structural so similarly named non-indexer projections stay trainable.
    """

    parts = name.split(".")
    for index, part in enumerate(parts):
        if part != "self_attention" or index + 1 >= len(parts):
            continue
        attention_parts = parts[index + 1 :]
        if attention_parts[0] in _INDEXER_DIRECT_SUBMODULE_NAMES:
            return True
        if "indexer" in attention_parts[:-1]:
            return True

# Adapt from https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/c3b20575d2bc815fcccd84bddb4c0401fc4b632b/verl/models/llama/megatron/layers/parallel_linear.py#L82
class LinearForLastLayer(torch.nn.Linear):
    # WORKSPACE CHANGE, part of the shared setup: `bias` defaults to False
    # here, where upstream slime v0.3.2 defaults it to True.
    #
    # Upstream cannot load a critic from a HuggingFace checkpoint at all. The
    # HF loader walks every Megatron parameter and asks the model's mapper for
    # a source tensor; `output_layer.weight` is special-cased (a [1, hidden]
    # value head is skipped when the HF tensor is [vocab, hidden]), but
    # `output_layer.bias` has no HF counterpart and no special case, so
    # `qwen_hf_tensor` raises KeyError("Unsupported Megatron parameter
    # 'output_layer.bias'") before training starts. See
    # slime/backends/megatron_utils/hf_to_megatron/{qwen,common}.py.
    #
    # A value head does not need a bias -- it is one scalar of freedom that
    # V(s) can equally express through the backbone -- and dropping it is the
    # smallest change that lets a critic start from HF weights, which is what
    # Stage B does.
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_size: int,
        output_size: int,
        *,
        config: TransformerConfig,
        bias: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(in_features=input_size, out_features=output_size, bias=bias)
        self.sequence_parallel = config.sequence_parallel
        if self.sequence_parallel:
            self.weight.sequence_parallel = True
            if bias:
                self.bias.sequence_parallel = True

        init_method_std = getattr(config, "init_method_std", None)
        if init_method_std is None:
            init_method_std = 0.02
        self.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=init_method_std)
        if bias:
            self.bias.data.zero_()

    def forward(
        self,
        input_: torch.Tensor,
        weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
        runtime_gather_output: bool | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None]:
        logits = super().forward(input_)
        logits = logits.float()
        if self.sequence_parallel:
            logits = tensor_parallel.gather_from_sequence_parallel_region(logits, tensor_parallel_output_grad=False)
        return logits, None


def _get_model_provider_func(
    args: argparse.Namespace,
    role: Literal["actor", "critic"] = "actor",
):
    # Support custom model provider path (similar to --custom-rm-path for reward models)
    if getattr(args, "custom_model_provider_path", None):

        def wrapped_model_provider(
            pre_process: bool = True, post_process: bool = True, vp_stage: int | None = None
        ) -> GPTModel:
            custom_model_provider = load_function(args.custom_model_provider_path)
            # Check if the custom provider supports vp_stage parameter
            has_vp_stage = "vp_stage" in inspect.signature(custom_model_provider).parameters
            if has_vp_stage:
                model = custom_model_provider(pre_process=pre_process, post_process=post_process, vp_stage=vp_stage)
            else:
                model = custom_model_provider(pre_process=pre_process, post_process=post_process)
            # Apply critic output layer if needed
            if post_process and role == "critic":
                model.output_layer = LinearForLastLayer(
                    input_size=model.config.hidden_size, output_size=1, config=model.config
                )
            return model

        return wrapped_model_provider

    def model_provider(pre_process: bool = True, post_process: bool = True, vp_stage: int | None = None) -> GPTModel:
        """Builds the model.

        If you set the use_legacy_models to True, it will return the legacy GPT model and if not the mcore GPT model.

        Args:
            pre_process (bool, optional): Set to true if you need to compute embedings. Defaults to True.
            post_process (bool, optional): Set to true if you need to want to compute output logits/loss. Defaults to True.


        Returns:
            Union[GPTModel, megatron.legacy.model.GPTModel]: The returned model
        """
        use_te = args.transformer_impl == "transformer_engine"

        # Experimental loading arguments from yaml
        config: TransformerConfig = core_transformer_config_from_args(args)
        # Older GLM Megatron forks consumed this flag from TransformerConfig.
        # Preserve that contract for custom specs, while freeze_model_params()
        # below provides the concrete implementation on current Megatron.
        config.freeze_indexer = getattr(args, "freeze_indexer", False)

        if args.spec is not None:
            transformer_layer_spec = import_module(args.spec)
            # Allow the spec to be a function so that user can use customized Megatron easier.
            if callable(transformer_layer_spec):
                result = transformer_layer_spec(args, config, vp_stage)
                # If the result is itself a model provider (callable with pre_process param),
                # delegate model construction to it directly (e.g. glm-omni VL model).
                if callable(result) and "pre_process" in inspect.signature(result).parameters:
                    model = result(pre_process=pre_process, post_process=post_process, vp_stage=vp_stage)
                    if post_process and role == "critic":
                        model.output_layer = LinearForLastLayer(
                            input_size=config.hidden_size, output_size=1, config=config
                        )
                    return model
                transformer_layer_spec = result
        else:
            if args.num_experts:
                # Define the decoder block spec
                kwargs = {
                    "use_transformer_engine": use_te,
                }
                if vp_stage is not None:
                    kwargs["vp_stage"] = vp_stage
                transformer_layer_spec = get_gpt_decoder_block_spec(config, **kwargs)
            else:
                # Define the decoder layer spec
                if use_te:
                    transformer_layer_spec = get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec(
                        num_experts=args.num_experts,
                        moe_grouped_gemm=args.moe_grouped_gemm,
                        qk_layernorm=args.qk_layernorm,
                        multi_latent_attention=args.multi_latent_attention,
                        moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm=args.moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm,
                    )
                else:
                    transformer_layer_spec = get_gpt_layer_local_spec(
                        num_experts=args.num_experts,
                        moe_grouped_gemm=args.moe_grouped_gemm,
                        qk_layernorm=args.qk_layernorm,
                        multi_latent_attention=args.multi_latent_attention,
                        moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm=args.moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm,
                    )

        build_model_context = nullcontext
        build_model_context_args = {}
        if args.fp8_param_gather:
            try:
                from transformer_engine.pytorch import fp8_model_init

                build_model_context = fp8_model_init
                build_model_context_args["enabled"] = True

                # Check if fp8_model_init supports preserve_high_precision_init_val
                if "preserve_high_precision_init_val" in inspect.signature(fp8_model_init).parameters:
                    build_model_context_args["preserve_high_precision_init_val"] = True
            except Exception as e:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "--fp8-param-gather requires `fp8_model_init` from TransformerEngine, but not found."
                ) from e

        kwargs = {
            "config": config,
            "transformer_layer_spec": transformer_layer_spec,
            "vocab_size": args.padded_vocab_size,
            "max_sequence_length": args.max_position_embeddings,
            "pre_process": pre_process,
            "post_process": post_process,
            "fp16_lm_cross_entropy": args.fp16_lm_cross_entropy,
            "parallel_output": True,
            "share_embeddings_and_output_weights": not args.untie_embeddings_and_output_weights,
            "position_embedding_type": args.position_embedding_type,
            "rotary_percent": args.rotary_percent,
            "rotary_base": args.rotary_base,
            "rope_scaling": args.use_rope_scaling,
        }

        if vp_stage is not None:
            kwargs["vp_stage"] = vp_stage

        if args.mtp_num_layers:
            from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import get_gpt_mtp_block_spec

            mtp_kwargs = {
                "use_transformer_engine": use_te,
            }
            if vp_stage is not None:
                mtp_kwargs["vp_stage"] = vp_stage

            mtp_block_spec = get_gpt_mtp_block_spec(config, transformer_layer_spec, **mtp_kwargs)
            kwargs["mtp_block_spec"] = mtp_block_spec

        with build_model_context(**build_model_context_args):
            model = GPTModel(**kwargs)

        if post_process and role == "critic":
            model.output_layer = LinearForLastLayer(input_size=config.hidden_size, output_size=1, config=config)

        return model

    return model_provider


def wrap_model_provider_with_freeze(original_provider, args):
    def wrapped_provider(
        pre_process=True,
        post_process=True,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        sig = inspect.signature(original_provider)
        provider_kwargs = {
            "pre_process": pre_process,
            "post_process": post_process,
        }
        for key in ["vp_stage", "config", "pg_collection"]:
            if key in sig.parameters:
                provider_kwargs[key] = kwargs.get(key, None)

        model = original_provider(**provider_kwargs)
        freeze_model_params(model, args)

        return model

    return wrapped_provider


def get_model_provider_func(args, role="actor"):
    return wrap_model_provider_with_freeze(_get_model_provider_func(args, role), args)


def freeze_model_params(model: GPTModel, args: argparse.Namespace):
    if getattr(args, "only_train_params_name_list", None):
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
            for pattern in args.only_train_params_name_list:
                if re.search(pattern, name):
                    param.requires_grad = True
                    break

    if getattr(args, "freeze_params_name_list", None):
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            for pattern in args.freeze_params_name_list:
                if re.search(pattern, name):
                    param.requires_grad = False
                    break

    if getattr(args, "freeze_indexer", False):
        frozen_indexer_params = []
        has_self_attention_params = False
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            has_self_attention_params |= "self_attention" in name.split(".")
            if _is_indexer_parameter(name):
                param.requires_grad = False
                frozen_indexer_params.append(name)

        if has_self_attention_params and not frozen_indexer_params:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "--freeze-indexer was requested, but this model chunk has self-attention "
                "parameters and no recognized DSA indexer parameters."
            )

        # Some pipeline stages may legitimately own no indexer weights, so an
        # empty local tuple is not itself an error.
        model._slime_frozen_indexer_param_names = tuple(frozen_indexer_params)
